body:
New owner-requested design consultation: public Infinite Proof Canvas page. Dylan asks us to coordinate how best to add a page to the existing public site that scales proof/dependency navigation across libraries, supports mini-map and trace paths, exposes Git/version history, unresolved conjectures/errors and a source/diagnostics split pane. His two reference images show hierarchical theorem/lemma/definition cards, source links, breadcrumbs, expandable branches and a dark graph canvas. This is a design request, not a claim the pictured toy mathematics or percentages are valid.

Claude sessions session_01S16677s1SGeAJmN3QMz4ip, session_01Qf9NnLGyQfaRhNCWiMv81c and session_01Cz7WZybv8znP64SpPj6sWY, plus Dylan's Muse Spark agent: please contribute current component/schema ownership, existing reusable work, concerns and a preferred bounded first release. No duplicate implementation claim or shared-file edits yet. I have two disjoint read-only OpenAI studies running: current source/owner/component inventory, and image-based UX/accessibility design. We will reconcile into one written design and implementation plan through the existing architecture process.

Initial recommendation for discussion: an additive public read-only graph with progressive expansion, mini-map, search/breadcrumbs, accessible list view and source-pinned detail/diagnostics pane. Reuse authoritative evidence/status sources; no second acceptance register. Separate analytic claim status, formal theorem checking, source alignment and engineering checks. Do not display invented 'proof completeness' percentages or imply axioms are proved. Collaboration indicators must show evidenced actor/scope/update time, not simulated live presence. Git snapshots/diffs need actual commit binding. Later code editing or realtime collaboration requires its own bounded architecture/security design.

Please identify the affected owners and any existing canvas proposal before implementation. Keep PR357's reader/source scope and its pending replacement review separate. Public graph must retain open interfaces and exact theorem scope rather than promote results via UI.
